title: Egg shape is caused by radial pressure of the oviduct before the shell hardens

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Egg shape is caused by radial pressure of the oviduct before the shell hardens

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The essential cause of the form and variation of form of an egg is the regularly varying, largely radial pressure applied by successive rings of the oviduct before the shell solidifies, not adaptation to nesting circumstances.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: this factor, the unknown but regularly varying, largely radial, pressure applied by successive annuli of the oviduct, is the essential cause of the form, and variations of form, of the egg.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Mechanical conformation of the egg”. Scope: birds' eggs and other hard-shelled eggs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-05: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed cause is testable in principle but not from existing egg image and trait databases. New longitudinal physiological and mechanical measurements are required for discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure ring-by-ring oviduct pressure and egg deformation before calcification across species and experimentally model whether those pressures predict final shape better than nesting ecology and intrinsic membrane properties. Accurate pressure-based prediction and weak independent nesting effects support the claim; the reverse refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim's 'essential cause' requires causal comparison with ecological alternatives.

No known public dataset contains pre-shell pressure fields linked to final egg form.

Pressure, membrane mechanics and secretion are jointly determined.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open comparative files are sufficient to ask whether nest type accounts for egg form once female anatomy is considered, which is the contrast Thompson draws with adaptation to nesting. They measure oviduct and pelvic size rather than the varying radial pressure he calls the essential cause. The negative claim about nesting can be examined now; the positive mechanical claim is only proxied, and locomotion-related anatomy remains entangled with it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare models that predict egg asymmetry and elongation from oviduct and pelvic dimensions with models that predict them from nest site and clutch arrangement. The anti-adaptation half is supported if nest variables add little once anatomy is included; the positive claim that radial oviduct pressure is the essential cause still requires a pressure measurement the anatomical sizes only proxy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Oviduct diameter and pelvic size are not the radial pressure of successive annuli.

Flight-related body shape is a third correlate that can mimic an oviduct effect.
